The orange square moved right! It moved from columns ~29-36 to columns ~36-43 (shifted 7 columns to the right). The orange is a movable player. It moved along the path to the right (toward B7).
So the game is: the orange square is the player, and it moves along the path (the black line) via arrow keys. The pegs are... what? Targets to collect? Obstacles?
The orange moved right by 7 columns (one "segment" of the path). The path from the orange to B7: the orange is at (31-39, 29-36)... it moved to (31-39, 36-43). B7 is at (15-19, 43-46). The path: orange → right → up → B7.
So the orange moves along the path. What happens when it reaches a peg? Maybe it collects it (the peg disappears). Goal: collect all the pegs? Or reach a specific location?
Wait, but the pegs are inside the box, and the path only touches the box at B7 and D1. So the orange can only reach the pegs at B7 and E1 (the pegs on the path). The other pegs (B2, B3, B5) are inside the box and unreachable by the orange... unless the orange can enter the box at B7 and move inside the box!
Hmm, wait. Maybe the orange can enter the box: at B7 the path connects to the box. If the orange moves up at B7, it enters the box and can move inside the box (through the 3×7 grid)! In that case, the orange could collect pegs inside the box.
But then what do the pegs' jump moves (the B2→B4 highlight) mean? Maybe the pegs move too (they jump), and the goal is to have the orange collect all the pegs, or to have the orange reach a goal cell.
Or: the pegs are obstacles, and the orange must navigate to a goal (e.g., the E1 cell or a specific cell).
